authorship.note: These fixtures freeze the mercurio.view.v1 <-> SysML v2 view map recorded in the plan's field-by-field table. They are a CONTRACT, not generated output: any increment that changes the map must change a fixture in the same commit.

tiers.1: Reifiable and interoperable. Standard scopes (expose + filter), the four standard renderings, viewpoints, composition. Direct lossless view-usage <-> mercurio.view.v1 map; renders in any conforming tool.
tiers.2: Reifiable but tool-specific. Non-standard view kinds and semantic-but-non-standard render params, carried by user rendering defs subtyping GraphicalRendering/TabularRendering plus one documented Mercurio metadata profile. Travels and versions; only Mercurio renders faithfully.
tiers.3: Not reified. SV-3 must return a typed NotReifiable naming the offending field rather than inventing an encoding.

round_trip_rules.tier1_tier2: spec -> usage -> spec is the identity.
round_trip_rules.materialized: A materialized save converts DiagramScopeDto::Traversal into ExplicitElements. That is a deliberate normalization, not a round-trip failure: assert materialize(spec) -> usage -> spec' == materialize(spec).
round_trip_rules.tier3: Returns NotReifiable naming the offending field.

Characterisation only, no expected spec. Records that import preserves the wildcard and drops the predicate, while expose drops both. SV-1 should route expose through the existing import path; the dropped predicate is a standing correctness bug on the import side too.

DiagramSpecDto has no explicit-element scope today; only TableScopeDto does. Without the additive DiagramScopeDto field there is no field to read a materialized diagram view back into, and the round-trip criterion is unsatisfiable for the whole diagram family.

Corrected 2026-08-28. This fixture originally wrote `view :>> columnView[1]` and `[2]` as if [n] indexed the columns. It does not: [n] is the multiplicity of the REDEFINING feature, and the pilot only ever writes one (Views Example.sysml:16-20). Two redefinitions of one feature collide, which is exactly what the compiler was reporting. Multiple columns are SUBSETS -- `view name :> columnView` -- because `:>` adds instances to a [0..*] feature while `:>>` replaces it. Column key/label (the column feature's declared name) is tier 1; TableColumnSpecDto.path is NOT -- the pilot column view carries only a `render`, so which attribute a column shows has no standard encoding and is tier 2 via the #Mercurio profile (V-6.4).
